# Troubleshooting

Find the message you saw. Each entry gives the exact text, what it means, and what to do.

## Server, engine and update messages (a09)

This section documents every message EZLM can show from the part of the program that
runs your model server (`internal/serve`), installs the AI engine and downloads models
(`internal/engine`), and checks for EZLM updates (`internal/update`).

Where you see them:

- **While EZLM sets up a model.** The setup screen lists the steps (engine, model,
  start, load, test). A failed step turns red, and the message is printed under it
  (`windows/EZLM/Install.cs:278`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:571`). The panel
  below the steps repeats the message and offers **Report this problem**
  (`windows/EZLM/Install.cs:154`).
- **While you start the server yourself.** Pressing **Start server** on Overview runs
  the same steps, so the same text appears there.
- **In Settings > Updates.** An update check that fails prints one line under the
  version, for example `EZLM 0.1.1. couldn't reach GitHub to check for updates.`
  (`windows/EZLM/SettingsPane.cs:65`). A failed update download prints its message on
  the small line under the update button (`windows/EZLM/SettingsPane.cs:318`).

Text is not translated. Everything in `code font` below is the exact wording, with
`<placeholders>` for the parts that change. A message in brackets at the end, like
`(Get "https://...": dial tcp: ...)`, is the original technical error. Leave it in
when you report the problem: it names the server and the reason.

### Starting and running the model server

#### the model server stopped while loading. Last log lines:
```
the model server stopped while loading. Last log lines:
<the last 8 lines of the server log>
```

**What it means:** the model server program quit while it was loading the model, and it
did not write one of the known error lines that EZLM recognises. The usual cause is a
graphics driver that crashes under load, or a start-up flag the build does not accept.
EZLM waits about 13 seconds to be sure (`internal/serve/client.go:90`, `:126`).

**What to do:** if you have an AMD Radeon or Intel Arc card, EZLM retries on the
processor by itself and the setup carries on, so you may only see a gold note about
it. On an NVIDIA card or a Mac, press **Resume and set it up**; if it stops in the same
place, send a report with the log lines. **Stop server**, then **Start server** also
retries without re-downloading.

Code: `internal/serve/client.go:97`, `:122`, `:126`.

#### the model did not finish loading in 10m0s. Last log lines:
```
the model did not finish loading in 10m0s. Last log lines:
<the last 8 lines of the server log>
```

**What it means:** the server process stayed alive for ten minutes without answering
`/health`, so EZLM gave up waiting. A very large model on a slow disk, or a model that
barely fits in memory, can take this long (`internal/serve/client.go:105`; the ten
minutes are set at `internal/app/app.go:817`).

**What to do:** press **Start server** on Overview and give it a few more minutes,
since a load that was nearly finished often completes. If it happens again, choose a
smaller model or the **Fastest** preference, and close other apps to free memory.

#### the running model server didn't stop. It was probably started with administrator rights, which EZLM can't override: restart your computer, or end "llama-server" in Task Manager, then try again

**What it means:** EZLM asked its server to stop and the server kept its port for ten
seconds. A server started by an administrator, or by another copy of EZLM, cannot be
ended by your normal user account (`internal/serve/config.go:196`, `:201`). This
appears while switching models, changing LAN mode or uninstalling.

**What to do:** restart the computer, or open Task Manager, find `llama-server`, choose
**End task**, then repeat what you were doing.

#### EZLM's settings file (<path>) is damaged: <reason>

**What it means:** `config.json` in EZLM's hidden folder cannot be read as JSON. It
holds your key, port, model and engine paths, so EZLM cannot start the server from it.
The path is `C:\Users\<you>\.ezlm\config.json` on Windows and
`~/.ezlm/config.json` on a Mac (`internal/paths/paths.go:10`, `:36`).

**What to do:** set the model up again (Models, then **Set it up**). EZLM writes
a fresh settings file and your model is reused from disk, so nothing is downloaded
twice. The key and port can change, so reconnect OpenCode, Hermes or DeepSeek Harness
afterwards. Keep the old file as `config.json.bak` if you want to report it.

Code: `internal/serve/config.go:61`.

#### couldn't open the server log: <reason>

**What it means:** EZLM could not create or open `~/.ezlm/logs/server.log` before
starting the server. A security app that locks the folder, a read-only disk, or a full
disk causes this (`internal/serve/service_windows.go:183`).

**What to do:** check that the disk is not full and that your antivirus allows EZLM's
hidden folder, then press **Start server**. If the file is locked by another program,
restart the computer.

#### couldn't start the server: <reason>

**What it means:** Windows accepted the request but the server program did not start.
The common cause is an antivirus or company security app blocking
`llama-server.exe`, or the file being quarantined between the check and the start
(`internal/serve/service_windows.go:200`).

**What to do:** open your antivirus quarantine, restore `llama-server.exe` and allow
EZLM's `bin` folder, then press **Start server**. EZLM downloads the engine again when
the program is missing.

#### launchctl bootstrap: <launchctl output>

**What it means:** macOS would not load EZLM's background service. The text is
launchctl's own wording, usually `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` or a
message that the service is already loaded (`internal/serve/service_darwin.go:35`).

**What to do:** quit EZLM, open it again, and press **Start server**. If it repeats,
log out of your Mac and back in, then try once more and report it if it still fails.

#### systemctl <command>: <systemctl output>

**What it means:** Linux's service manager refused the command, for example
`Failed to restart ezlm.service: Unit ezlm.service not found` or `Access denied`
(`internal/serve/service_linux.go:20`).

**What to do:** run `systemctl --user daemon-reload` in a terminal, then press
**Start server** again. If the message says access denied, check that you are logged
in to a desktop session with a user service manager, then report it.

#### test request failed: <HTTP status>

**What it means:** the server is running and accepted the request, but the model
answered with an error instead of a reply, for example
`test request failed: 500 Internal Server Error`. The context window being full, or
the model failing on that prompt, produces this (`internal/serve/client.go:184`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up**, which repeats the test. If it fails again,
stop the server, start it, and report with the log lines from Logs.

#### test request returned no answer

**What it means:** the reply arrived but contained no choices at all, which means the
server sent an empty response (`internal/serve/client.go:201`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up**. If it happens again, report it with the
server log.

#### the model answered with nothing

**What it means:** the model returned an empty answer with no thinking text either.
Some models do this on a short prompt (`internal/serve/client.go:208`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up**, or open **Chat** and ask a question. If
every answer is empty, switch to another model and report it.

#### (Your model is thinking out loud and working. Ask it something in the chat.)

**What it means:** not an error. The model produced only thinking text and no final
answer, so EZLM shows this sentence instead of an empty reply box
(`internal/serve/client.go:210`).

**What to do:** ask it something in **Chat**. The model is working; a longer or
clearer question usually gets a final answer.

#### A line from the server log, quoted with no prefix

**What it means:** EZLM watches the log for seven known fatal phrases and, when it
finds one, shows that log line as the message, so the text is llama.cpp's own wording
(`internal/serve/client.go:128`, `:134`). The phrases and what they mean:

- `failed to load model` or `error loading model`: the model file is damaged or
  incomplete. Pick the model again so EZLM downloads it again.
- `out of memory` or `failed to allocate`: not enough free memory at that moment.
  Close other apps with **Free up memory**, or choose a smaller model.
- `address already in use` or `couldn't bind`: another program holds the port. EZLM
  usually moves to a free port by itself; if you see this, restart the computer and
  try again.
- `exiting due to`: the server shut itself down. Report the line, since it names the
  reason above it in Logs.

**What to do:** the action depends on the phrase, as listed. Press **Resume and set it up**
after the fix.

#### Raw system errors from the server

**What it means:** when nothing more specific applies, the message is the operating
system's own text, for example `open C:\Users\me\.ezlm\config.json: Access is denied.`
or `fork/exec ...: permission denied`. These come from reading the settings, writing
the service file or launching the program, and EZLM passes them through unchanged
(`internal/serve/config.go:62`, `internal/serve/run.go:26`,
`internal/serve/service_darwin.go:82`).

**What to do:** read the path in the message. If it is inside EZLM's folder, allow
that folder in your security app and check the disk is not full, then try again.

### Installing the AI engine

EZLM normally uses a fixed, tested llama.cpp build, so these steps do not ask GitHub
for anything (`internal/engine/pinned.go:3`). The first three messages only appear
when `EZLM_LLAMA=latest` is set.

#### could not reach GitHub for llama.cpp: <HTTP status>

**What it means:** EZLM asked GitHub for the newest llama.cpp release and got an error
or a non-200 answer. GitHub allows 60 requests an hour per address, so `403 Forbidden`
often means the limit was reached (`internal/engine/engine.go:60`).

**What to do:** EZLM keeps using the engine already on disk when it can. If there is
none, wait an hour and press **Resume and set it up**, or unset `EZLM_LLAMA` so EZLM uses
its tested build.

#### llama.cpp release <tag> has no downloadable builds

**What it means:** the release GitHub calls newest has no program files for any
computer, and no file naming a nightly build (`internal/engine/engine.go:95`). This is
a problem at llama.cpp's end, not on your computer.

**What to do:** unset `EZLM_LLAMA` so EZLM uses its tested build, then press **Set it
up again**. Report the message if it persists.

#### no llama.cpp build for <os>/<arch> (<backend>) in release <tag>

**What it means:** the release has no archive matching your operating system,
processor type and graphics backend. EZLM names all three in the message
(`internal/engine/engine.go:189`).

**What to do:** report it with the exact line. As a workaround, choose the **Fastest**
preference, which installs a processor-only build where one exists.

#### unpacking <archive>: <reason>

**What it means:** the download finished but could not be unpacked, usually because
the archive is truncated or the disk refused a write (`internal/engine/engine.go:255`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up**. If the same file is named twice, delete it
from EZLM's `bin` folder (`C:\Users\<you>\.ezlm\bin` or `~/.ezlm/bin`) and retry, or
report it.

#### llama-server not found in <archive>

**What it means:** the archive unpacked but did not contain the server program. The
build itself is wrong (`internal/engine/engine.go:261`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up** once. If it repeats, report it: EZLM cannot
fix this on your computer.

#### checksum mismatch for <file>

**What it means:** the downloaded file's SHA-256 does not match the value GitHub
published, so EZLM deleted it and did not install it (`internal/engine/engine.go:320`,
`:335`; for an EZLM update the same check is at `internal/update/update.go:120`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up**. If it happens twice on the same file, a
proxy or antivirus is altering downloads, so try another network or allow
`github.com` and `huggingface.co`, then report it.

#### unsafe path in archive: <name>

**What it means:** an entry in the archive points outside the folder it should unpack
into, so EZLM refused it (`internal/engine/engine.go:341`). This is a damaged or
tampered archive.

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up**, and report it if it repeats. Do not unpack
the file by hand.

### Downloading a model or the engine

Downloads resume where they stopped, retry five times without progress, and wait 45
seconds for data before cutting a stalled connection
(`internal/engine/download.go:21`, `:78`). The messages below end with the original
technical error in brackets.

#### the download keeps stalling (no data arrives for a long time). Check the internet connection and try again: EZLM picks up where it stopped (<error>)

**What it means:** the connection stayed open but delivered nothing for 45 seconds,
five times in a row (`internal/engine/download.go:223`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up**. If it stalls again, try another network
(a phone hotspot is fine), since some networks and VPNs throttle large downloads.

#### this computer can't find the download server (<host>), so it looks offline. Check the internet connection and try again: EZLM picks up where it stopped (<error>)

**What it means:** the name of the download server did not resolve, so EZLM cannot
reach it (`internal/engine/download.go:225`).

**What to do:** check that you are online and that no VPN or DNS blocker is running,
then press **Resume and set it up**. Nothing already downloaded is lost.

#### the download server's security certificate looks expired, which usually means this computer's date and time are wrong. Set the clock right in your system settings and try again (<error>)

**What it means:** the certificate check failed because it is past its expiry date,
which normally means the computer's clock is wrong
(`internal/engine/download.go:227`).

**What to do:** set the date and time to update automatically, then press **Resume and set it up**.

#### something on this network (a security app, antivirus or company proxy) is intercepting secure connections, so the download can't be trusted. Try another network, or allow huggingface.co and github.com in that app (<error>)

**What it means:** the certificate presented for the download does not belong to the
server EZLM asked for, which is what a proxy that inspects traffic looks like
(`internal/engine/download.go:229`).

**What to do:** allow `huggingface.co` and `github.com` in the security app, or
disconnect from the company network and press **Resume and set it up**.

#### the connection to the download server keeps dropping. Check the internet connection and try again: EZLM picks up where it stopped (<error>)

**What it means:** connections opened and then broke before any progress, five times
in a row (`internal/engine/download.go:231`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up** and leave it running. A download that keeps
making progress never gives up, so a flaky line still finishes.

#### <file> isn't on the download server any more (it may have been moved or renamed). Pick another model, or report this problem

**What it means:** the server answered 404 or 410, and EZLM stopped retrying at once
because a missing file will not come back (`internal/engine/download.go:241`).

**What to do:** pick another model, or the same model at another size. Report it so
the catalog can be corrected.

#### the download server won't hand out <file> (it may now need an account). Pick another model, or report this problem

**What it means:** the server answered 401 or 403, which usually means the file now
requires a login or the link has expired (`internal/engine/download.go:243`).

**What to do:** pick another model, or report it. Retrying the same link will not
help.

#### downloading <file> failed: <HTTP status>

**What it means:** the server refused the request with a client error other than the
ones above, for example `416` or `451` (`internal/engine/download.go:245`).

**What to do:** report it with the status in the message, then pick another model if
you need to be running quickly.

#### the download server is having trouble (<HTTP status>). Try again in a few minutes: EZLM resumes where it stopped

**What it means:** the server answered with a temporary error such as
`503 Service Unavailable`, and EZLM has already retried five times
(`internal/engine/download.go:247`).

**What to do:** wait a few minutes and press **Resume and set it up**. The partial file is
kept and the download continues from there.

#### the downloaded file came out the wrong size (<got> bytes instead of <want>), so EZLM deleted it. Try again, and if it happens again, report this problem

**What it means:** the transfer reported success but the file is not the size the
catalog says, so EZLM removed the partial file rather than use it
(`internal/engine/download.go:87`, `:94`).

**What to do:** press **Resume and set it up**, which starts that file from zero. If it
repeats, report it, since it usually means a proxy is rewriting the download.

#### the disk filled up during the download. Free about <n> GB and press Set it up again: EZLM resumes where it stopped

**What it means:** the write failed with a disk-full error. EZLM turns that into this
sentence, which is the one place a raw `no space left on device` becomes readable
(`internal/app/app.go:744`).

**What to do:** free the space it names (empty the Trash, remove large files, or move
models to another drive in Settings), then press **Resume and set it up**.

### Updating EZLM

The update check runs when you open Settings, and the result is reused for an hour
(`internal/app/settings.go:36`).

#### couldn't reach GitHub to check for updates

**What it means:** the request to GitHub's release list failed outright, so EZLM has
no version to compare against (`internal/update/update.go:67`). On screen the line
reads `EZLM 0.1.1. couldn't reach GitHub to check for updates.` on Windows and
`EZLM 0.1.1. Couldn't reach GitHub to check for updates.` on a Mac, because each app
capitalises the sentence (`windows/EZLM/SettingsPane.cs:66`,
`macos/Sources/EZLM/Settings.swift:296`).

**What to do:** check the internet connection, then press **Check for updates**. Your
model keeps running while you do.

#### checking for updates failed (<HTTP status>)

**What it means:** GitHub answered with a non-200 status, for example
`403 Forbidden` when the hourly request limit for your address is used up
(`internal/update/update.go:72`).

**What to do:** wait up to an hour and press **Check for updates**. The rest of EZLM
is unaffected.

#### couldn't read the release list

**What it means:** the answer arrived but was not the JSON EZLM expects, usually
because a proxy or security app replaced the page (`internal/update/update.go:89`).

**What to do:** press **Check for updates** once more. If it repeats, allow
`api.github.com` in your security app and report it.

#### checksum mismatch for EZLM-Setup-<version>.exe (or .dmg)

**What it means:** the downloaded installer did not match GitHub's published SHA-256,
so EZLM deleted it and did not run it (`internal/update/update.go:120`).

**What to do:** press the update button again. If it repeats, download the installer from
the releases page yourself and run it. Your models are kept.

#### Update download messages

The installer download uses the same download code as models, so every message in the
section above can appear here with an installer file name. On Windows the message is
printed on the small line under the update button
(`windows/EZLM/SettingsPane.cs:318`). **What to do** is the same in each case, with
one addition: if the message names a full disk, free space in your temporary folder
as well, since the installer is downloaded there (`internal/update/update.go:112`).

### Messages that are not user-facing

These exist in the three packages but are swallowed before they reach a screen, so a
tester cannot see them. They are listed so the next agent does not re-document them.

- `/props answered <status>` (`internal/serve/props.go:38`): `refreshProps` ignores
  it and keeps the previous values (`internal/app/connect.go:89`).
- Errors from reading the server start time (`internal/serve/client.go:217`) and from
  listing EZLM's own server processes (`internal/serve/procs.go:15`): both fall back
  to a default.
- `the download stopped receiving data` (`internal/engine/download.go:34`): always
  wrapped by the stalling message above.
- `context canceled` (`internal/engine/download.go:63`): the user pressed
  **Cancel**, and the setup screen says `Cancelled` instead.

### Related messages from other packages

Two app-level messages wrap these texts and are worth cross-referencing, because a
tester sees them instead of the original:

- `the model server couldn't start: <reason>` adds the most telling line from the
  server log (`internal/app/app.go:1469`, `:1550`).
- `your model server didn't start: <first line>. Press Start server on Overview to
  try again` is used when connecting an app
  (`internal/app/connect.go:79`).
- `EZLM's model server program is missing and couldn't be restored (<reason>). If an
  antivirus app removed it, allow the folder <path> in that app, then press Start
  server` wraps an engine install failure (`internal/app/app.go:1541`).

## Troubleshooting: machine scan, model fit and the model list

This section covers the messages produced by the code that looks at your computer
(`internal/scan`), the code that decides which model runs well on it
(`internal/fit`), and the model list EZLM ships and updates (`internal/catalog`).

Two things are worth knowing before you read the entries.

First, none of these three parts of EZLM ever stops the app. The scan always
returns a result, and anything it could not read becomes a note or a zero. The
fit code always answers yes or no for each model. The catalog always falls back
to the copy built into the app. So most of the failures below are silent, and
the entry tells you what you see instead of a message.

Second, the notes the scan writes are only printed by the command line program
(`ezlm scan`). The Windows and Mac apps read them but never show them, so a
tester using the app will not see the two "Note" messages below
(`windows/EZLM/Models.cs:28` declares the field, and no app file reads it;
`cmd/ezlm/main.go:376` prints it).

### Entries from the machine scan

#### "No supported GPU found: models will run on the CPU, which is slower."

**What it means.** EZLM looked for a graphics card in three ways and found none
it can use: `nvidia-smi` did not answer, `rocm-smi` did not answer, and Windows
did not report an AMD or Intel card that qualifies. Models still run, on the
processor, at a few words per second. The message is written once, in
`internal/scan/scan_other.go:18`.

**What to do.** On an NVIDIA machine, open a terminal and run `nvidia-smi`. If
that command is not found, reinstall the graphics driver from the vendor and
choose the option that adds its tools to the path. On an AMD machine with
Windows, check that the card is listed in Task Manager under Performance. On
Linux with an AMD card, install the ROCm tools so `rocm-smi` exists. Then scan
again.

#### "Intel Mac detected: models will run on the CPU."

**What it means.** The Mac has an Intel processor, so there is no shared
graphics memory to use and EZLM does not offer the Metal build. Everything runs
on the processor. The message is written in `internal/scan/scan_darwin.go:12`,
and the scan returns early there, so an Intel Mac also shows no graphics card
at all.

**What to do.** Pick the smallest model in the list and expect slow replies. If
the Mac is Apple Silicon and this message appears, the app was built for the
wrong processor, so download the Apple Silicon build.

#### No message: a card is present but EZLM does not list it

**What it means.** A graphics card can be skipped without any message. On
Windows, an AMD or Intel card only counts when its name looks like a discrete
model (Radeon RX, Radeon Pro, Arc A or B) and it has at least 2 GB of its own
memory, or when it is built-in graphics with 8 GB or more set aside. Everyday
built-in graphics are left out on purpose because they are about as fast as the
processor (`internal/scan/gpu_discrete.go:203` to `224`). A card whose driver
entry has no name, or whose driver key cannot be read, is also dropped
(`internal/scan/display_windows.go:49` to `92`).

**What to do.** If the card is real and recent, update its driver, then scan
again. If it is built-in graphics with a small memory share, expect the
processor path and pick a small model.

#### No message: the NVIDIA driver is installed but `nvidia-smi` fails

**What it means.** The scan runs `nvidia-smi` and treats any failure as "no
NVIDIA card" (`internal/scan/gpu_discrete.go:15` to `18`). A driver that is
mid-update, a card in a broken power state, or a machine where the tool is not
on the path all end the same way: EZLM carries on to AMD, then to the Windows
display list, and usually ends at the processor.

**What to do.** Run `nvidia-smi` yourself. If it prints a card, scan again. If
it prints an error, reinstall the driver and reboot.

#### No message: memory or disk numbers show as zero

**What it means.** Each reading in the scan is best effort. If the memory call
fails, total and free memory stay at zero, and the fit code then assumes a
2 GB reserve for the system (`internal/fit/fit.go:204` to `209`). If the disk
call fails, free space stays at zero, and every model is marked as having
enough room, because a zero free space is read as "unknown" rather than "full"
(`internal/fit/fit.go:321`). `internal/scan/scan.go:280` to `289` has the same
effect for a model folder on a drive that cannot be read: free space comes back
as zero.

**What to do.** Scan again. If the numbers stay at zero, the drive or the
memory reading is being blocked, often by security software, so check that
first. Do not trust the "enough room" claim while the disk figure reads zero.

#### "process does not exist"

**What it means.** You asked EZLM to close a program and the program was already
gone by the time the request arrived. The text comes from the process library
EZLM uses, through `internal/scan/scan.go:260` to `262`, and the app shows it
as the note in the close dialog (`windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:495`,
`macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:339`).

**What to do.** Nothing is wrong. Scan again to refresh the list.

#### "operation not permitted"

**What it means.** The program is running under another user account, or it is
one of the protected programs (the operating system, security software, remote
access, or EZLM itself), so the safety rules refused to close it. The rule is
applied again at close time in `internal/scan/scan.go:264`, and the rules
themselves are in `internal/scan/apps.go:183` to `231`.

**What to do.** Close it yourself from its own window, or leave it open and pick
a smaller model.

#### No error: closing a program needs a second, forceful attempt

**What it means.** Closing is gentle first, the same as clicking the window's
close button. A program with no window, or one that ignores the request, comes
back with "needs force" instead of an error
(`internal/scan/apps.go:120` to `122`, `internal/scan/apps.go:154`). The
wording of that prompt belongs to the app, not to this code.

**What to do.** Choose the forceful close, and save your work in that program
first if it has any.

#### No message: graphics memory reads zero for a moment after start

**What it means.** On Windows with an AMD or Intel card, the first live reading
of graphics memory starts a background lookup and returns zero until it
finishes (`internal/scan/display_windows.go:113` to `137`). The dashboard can
show zero free for a second or two.

**What to do.** Wait a moment and let the reading catch up. If it stays at zero,
run a scan.

### Entries from the model fit

The fit code has no messages of its own. It answers "yes" or "no" for each
model, and the app turns a "no" into one of the sentences below. All of them
mean the same thing: no arrangement of that model fits in the memory that is
free right now.

#### "No model fits in the memory that's free right now. Quit an app on the right, then scan again."

**What it means.** Every model in the list failed. The app builds this sentence
from an empty plan list (`windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:410`); the Mac version says
"No model fits in the memory that's free right now." (`macos/Sources/EZLM/Wizard.swift:190`),
and the command line says "No model fits right now. Close some apps or free
disk space and scan again." (`cmd/ezlm/main.go:384`). The fit code returns
nothing when no quant of no model fits (`internal/fit/fit.go:288` to `293`).

**What to do.** Close the biggest programs in the list on the right, then scan
again. If that is not enough, the machine is below the smallest model EZLM
knows; a machine with 8 GB of memory can still run a small model, so check that
free memory is not near zero before giving up.

#### "model \"qwen3.8-27b\" doesn't fit this machine"

**What it means.** You asked for a model by name and it was not in the plan list
from the last scan (`internal/app/app.go:635`). Either it does not fit, or the
scan is older than a memory change.

**What to do.** Scan again, then pick the model from the list instead of by
name.

#### "Qwen3.8 27B doesn't fit this machine right now"

**What it means.** You switched to a model that is in the list but has no
working arrangement at this moment, for example because another program took
the free memory since the scan (`internal/app/app.go:1155`).

**What to do.** Close a program, scan again, then switch.

#### "Qwen3.8 27B (Q4_K_M) doesn't fit in the memory that's free right now"

**What it means.** The model has other files that fit, but this particular file
does not (`internal/app/app.go:1163`). Larger files of the same model need
more memory.

**What to do.** Pick a smaller file of the same model, which the model list
offers, or close a program first.

#### "not enough disk" and "Heads up: this needs about 40 GB and 12 GB is free. Make room now (empty the Trash, remove big files) or the download will pause when the disk fills."

**What it means.** The model fits in memory but not on the drive. Free space
below the download size plus 2 GB marks a plan this way
(`internal/fit/fit.go:321`). A plan is still offered, because you can make room
while it downloads (`internal/fit/fit.go:285` to `287`). The command line shows
"not enough disk" beside the row (`cmd/ezlm/main.go:393`), and the app prints
the longer sentence before it starts downloading (`internal/app/app.go:735`).

**What to do.** Free the space named in the message, then set the model up
again. A download that was interrupted resumes where it stopped.

#### No message: a model is offered but marked slow

**What it means.** Plans below 8 words per second are labelled "slow"
(`internal/fit/fit.go:487` to `494`). They are still offered and ranked last
(`internal/fit/fit.go:249` to `257`), so a machine with very little free memory
can still run something. With the "smartest" preference, a plan below 5 words
per second on a graphics card, or 2 on the processor, counts as unusable
(`internal/fit/fit.go:80`).

**What to do.** Expect a long wait for each reply, or pick a smaller model.

### Entries from the model list

#### "catalog has no models"

**What it means.** A model list file parsed correctly but contained no models
(`internal/catalog/catalog.go:196`). In practice you only see this in one
place: if the copy built into the app is broken, EZLM stops at startup with
"embedded catalog is invalid: catalog has no models"
(`internal/catalog/catalog.go:161` to `164`). That is a build fault, not
something a tester can cause.

**What to do.** Reinstall the app. If the app starts and the list is simply
empty, report it, because the built-in list is the last fallback and should
never be empty.

#### No message: a model list file given by `EZLM_CATALOG` is ignored

**What it means.** Setting `EZLM_CATALOG` to a file path makes EZLM read that
file instead of the built-in list, which is meant for development. If the file
cannot be read, or does not parse, or has no models, EZLM quietly uses the
built-in list (`internal/catalog/catalog.go:149` to `155`). There is no
message either way.

**What to do.** If you set that variable and the list does not change, check
the path and the JSON, or unset the variable.

#### No message: the online model list is not used

**What it means.** EZLM tries to fetch a newer model list once, with a four
second limit (`internal/catalog/catalog.go:166`). Offline, behind a firewall,
or on a slow connection, the fetch fails and the built-in list is used. A
fetched list is only accepted when it has models and a higher version number
than the built-in one (`internal/catalog/catalog.go:174`). All of these cases
are silent.

**What to do.** Nothing. The built-in list is complete and correct for this
version. A missing update only means a newer model may not appear yet, so
update the app to get it.

#### "embedded catalog is invalid: ..." at startup

**What it means.** The model list compiled into the app could not be parsed, so
there is nothing to fall back to and EZLM stops (`internal/catalog/catalog.go:161`
to `164`).

**What to do.** Reinstall the app, and report the message, because it means the
release itself was built wrong.

### Open questions for the guide lead

- The two scan notes are invisible in both apps. Either the apps should show
  them, or this section should stop calling them messages a tester can see.
- Several fit sentences name the model and the file, and the exact text varies
  with the model. Keep the shape and treat the names as examples.

## Troubleshooting: page, keys, helper processes, sleep, requirements, version

This section covers the messages produced by `internal/web`, `internal/keys`, `internal/proc`,
`internal/awake`, `internal/prereq` and `internal/version`. Some are shown in the browser page, some
in the app's setup list, and some only reach the log. Each entry gives the exact text, what it means,
and what to do.

A note on where the text appears:

- The browser page shows `internal/web` messages as plain page text or as a red error line.
- `internal/prereq` results appear in the app's setup check list as a name, a detail line and an
  action line (`internal/prereq/prereq.go:26-33`).
- `internal/proc` and `internal/awake` never draw on screen. Their errors are wrapped by the caller
  (usually `internal/integrate`) or written to the log.

### The browser page (`internal/web`)

#### 1. `forbidden`

**Message:** `forbidden` (plain page text, HTTP 403)
**Meaning:** The page was opened under a name that is not the exact address EZLM is listening on. EZLM
only answers requests addressed to its own `127.0.0.1:<port>` (`internal/web/server.go:232-237`), which
stops a web page on another site from talking to your local EZLM. Typing `localhost:<port>` instead of
the printed `127.0.0.1:<port>` triggers it, and so does opening the address from another machine.
**Action:** Close the tab and open the Setup page address that EZLM printed, or start EZLM again so it
opens the right one for you.
**Code:** `internal/web/server.go:234` (verified: a request with `Host: localhost:<port>` returns
403 `forbidden`).

#### 2. `this page is out of date: reopen EZLM`

**Message:** `this page is out of date: reopen EZLM` (HTTP 401). The page shows it as
`This page is out of date. Close it and open EZLM again.` when the response body has no other error.
**Meaning:** Every EZLM launch makes a new secret and puts it in the page address. A tab left open
from an earlier launch, or a bookmark without the secret, sends an old or missing secret
(`internal/web/server.go:247-260`).
**Action:** Close the tab and start EZLM again, then use the page it opens.
**Code:** `internal/web/server.go:255`; page fallback text `internal/web/static/app.js:20` (verified:
a request with no token, and one with a wrong token, both return 401 with this text).

#### 3. A red line with an action's own reason, for example `the disk filled up during the download.`

**Message:** whatever the action reported, as `{"error": "<reason>"}` with HTTP 400
(`internal/web/server.go:262-273`). The page prints that reason in a red line and, during setup, adds
`Stopped` plus a `Back to the start` button (`internal/web/static/app.js:586-592`).
**Meaning:** The request reached EZLM and EZLM refused it. The text is the real reason, passed
through unchanged, so the wording varies by action. A real example is `the disk filled up during the
download. Free about 6 GB and press Set it up again: EZLM resumes where it stopped`
(`internal/app/app.go:744`).
**Action:** Read the reason in the red line and do what it names. If it mentions space, free some
disk. If it mentions a file or folder, choose a different storage folder. If it mentions a port, close
whatever else is using it and try again.
**Code:** `internal/web/server.go:266-269`; `internal/app/app.go:744`.

#### 4. `streaming unsupported`

**Message:** `streaming unsupported` (plain page text, HTTP 500)
**Meaning:** The browser connection cannot carry live progress, so EZLM cannot stream setup steps to
the page. It is rare and means the page is being served through something other than the normal
built-in server (`internal/web/server.go:275-280`).
**Action:** Reload the page once. If it comes back, close EZLM, start it again and reopen the page.
**Code:** `internal/web/server.go:278`.

#### 5. A startup failure such as `listen tcp 127.0.0.1:0: bind: ...`

**Message:** the operating system's own text, printed by the command line as `ezlm: <text>`
(`cmd/ezlm/main.go:203-206`), or handed to the app in engine mode (`cmd/ezlm/main.go:232-235`).
**Meaning:** EZLM could not open its local port at all, so there is no page. The port is chosen
automatically (`internal/web/server.go:75`), so this points at the system, not at a clash with
another program: too many open connections, a security tool blocking loopback, or a broken network
stack.
**Action:** Restart the computer and try again. If it repeats, allow EZLM in your security software
and report the exact text.
**Code:** `internal/web/server.go:74-83`.

#### 6. The page opens but sits on `Processor` forever

**Message:** no error text, the scan list never fills in.
**Meaning:** The page asked for the machine scan and the request did not come back. Because the
page's own request has no time limit, a stuck scan looks like a frozen list
(`internal/web/static/app.js:249-252`, `:263-275`).
**Action:** Wait a minute. If nothing changes, close the page, quit EZLM and start it again.
**Code:** `internal/web/server.go:90-96` (scan endpoint), `internal/web/static/app.js:249`.

### Keys (`internal/keys`)

#### 7. `panic: <random source error>`

**Message:** a Go panic, for example `panic: read /dev/urandom: input/output error`
(`internal/keys/keys.go:16-19`).
**Meaning:** The system's random number generator failed while EZLM was making an API key. EZLM
panics rather than hand out a weak key (`internal/keys/keys.go:12-22`). This is very rare and means
the operating system itself is unhealthy.
**Action:** Restart the computer and start EZLM again. If it repeats, report the exact panic text.
**Code:** `internal/keys/keys.go:16-19`.

#### 8. A key that looks wrong

**Message:** no message. The key does not start with `ezlm-`, or is shorter than the usual length.
**Meaning:** Every key EZLM makes is `ezlm-` plus 40 letters and digits, about 238 bits
(`internal/keys/keys.go:11-22`). A key without the prefix was typed or copied wrongly, or came from
another tool.
**Action:** Copy the key again with the page's copy button, and paste it whole, with no spaces before
or after.
**Code:** `internal/keys/keys.go:22`.

### Helper processes (`internal/proc`)

These messages reach you only through the feature that ran the helper, usually as part of a longer
sentence such as `the installer stopped with this message: ...` (`internal/integrate/installer.go:69`).
The log holds the full command and output.

#### 9. `exec: "<name>": executable file not found in $PATH`

**Message:** `exec: "npm": executable file not found in $PATH`, with the real program name in place
of `npm`.
**Meaning:** The helper program EZLM wanted to run is not installed, or is installed somewhere EZLM
cannot see. This is the start failure from `internal/proc/proc.go:62-64`.
**Action:** Install the program the message names, or reopen EZLM from a normal desktop session so it
sees your usual `PATH`, then try the action again.
**Code:** `internal/proc/proc.go:62-64`.

#### 10. `exit status 1`, `exit status 2`, or another number

**Message:** `exit status 1` (the number is the program's own exit code).
**Meaning:** The helper ran and decided to fail. The reason is in its output, which EZLM writes to
the log (`internal/proc/proc.go:77-83`).
**Action:** Open the log from the error line's `Details` and read the last lines of the helper's
output, then follow what that output says.
**Code:** `internal/proc/proc.go:76-83`.

#### 11. `signal: killed`

**Message:** `signal: killed`
**Meaning:** EZLM stopped the helper and everything it started, either because you pressed Cancel or
because the step ran out of time (`internal/proc/proc.go:84-88`).
**Action:** Start the action again and let it run without cancelling. If it keeps timing out, close
other programs to free memory and try once more.
**Code:** `internal/proc/proc.go:84-88`.

#### 12. `context deadline exceeded` or `context canceled`

**Message:** `context deadline exceeded` (ran out of time) or `context canceled` (you cancelled).
**Meaning:** The step hit its time limit or you stopped it, and EZLM killed the helper's whole process
tree so nothing is left running behind it (`internal/proc/proc.go:1-4`, `:84-88`).
**Action:** Start the action again and leave it alone. If it keeps timing out, use a faster connection
or free disk space first.
**Code:** `internal/proc/proc.go:87`.

#### 13. A step that "finishes" while a helper is still running

**Message:** no message.
**Meaning:** Some installers deliberately leave a background service running. EZLM stops reading
their output after 5 seconds and treats the step as done, so a progress line can stop moving while the
service is still starting (`internal/proc/proc.go:47-50`, `:80-82`).
**Action:** Wait a few seconds and reload the page. If the app still shows not connected, use its own
`Check` or `Test` button.
**Code:** `internal/proc/proc.go:50`, `:80-82`.

### Keeping the computer awake (`internal/awake`)

#### 14. The computer went to sleep during a download

**Message:** none. `awake` fails silently by design (`internal/awake/awake.go:1-4`, `:11-15`).
**Meaning:** EZLM asks the system to stay awake only while a long job runs. On a Mac it starts
`/usr/bin/caffeinate` (`internal/awake/awake_darwin.go:11-14`), on Linux it starts
`systemd-inhibit` (`internal/awake/awake_linux.go:10-13`), and on Windows it makes a power request
(`internal/awake/awake_windows.go:33-49`). If the tool is missing, or the system refuses, the job
carries on and the computer may sleep. Closing the lid or choosing Sleep still sleeps on purpose.
**Action:** Leave the lid open and avoid choosing Sleep during setup, or change your sleep setting to
a longer time for the download.
**Code:** `internal/awake/awake.go:11-15`; `internal/app/app.go:592`.

### What your machine needs (`internal/prereq`)

The app shows these as a check list. A `fix` item is handled by EZLM. A `fail` item stops setup
until you act (`internal/prereq/prereq.go:19-24`, `internal/app/app.go:646-658`).

#### 15. `Not installed. The AI engine needs it.`

**Message:** `Microsoft Visual C++ runtime` / `Not installed. The AI engine needs it.` with the
action `EZLM will install it from Microsoft (Windows asks for permission once).`
**Meaning:** The AI engine's Windows build needs Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime and it is missing
(`internal/prereq/prereq.go:96-98`).
**Action:** Approve the Windows permission prompt when setup offers to install it, and let setup
continue.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:96-98`; installer `internal/prereq/prereq.go:183-194`.

#### 16. `Version 14.29.30133 is older than the engine needs (14.51.36247).`

**Message:** `Version <found> is older than the engine needs (<14.51.36247>).` with the action
`EZLM will update it from Microsoft (Windows asks for permission once).`
**Meaning:** The runtime is installed but too old for the engine (`internal/prereq/prereq.go:99-101`).
**Action:** Approve the Windows permission prompt and let EZLM update it.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:99-101`.

#### 17. `Couldn't install the Visual C++ runtime: <reason>`

**Message:** `Couldn't install the Visual C++ runtime: <reason>`
**Meaning:** EZLM tried to download and run Microsoft's installer and either the download failed or
the installer failed. Windows needs permission for this, so a dismissed prompt ends up here
(`internal/app/app.go:651-654`).
**Action:** Run setup again and click Yes on the Windows permission prompt. If it repeats, install the
runtime yourself from the link the check list shows and run setup again.
**Code:** `internal/app/app.go:651-654`; `internal/prereq/prereq.go:183-194`.

#### 18. `macOS version` / `Update to macOS 13.3 or newer in System Settings > General > Software Update.`

**Message:** detail `macOS 13.1`, action `Update to macOS 13.3 or newer in System Settings >
General > Software Update.`
**Meaning:** The Mac's system version is older than the AI engine supports
(`internal/prereq/prereq.go:109-118`).
**Action:** Update macOS in System Settings > General > Software Update, then run setup again.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:112-116`.

#### 19. `Couldn't read the glibc version.`

**Message:** `System libraries (glibc)` / `Couldn't read the glibc version.`
**Meaning:** EZLM could not ask the system which C library version it has. Setup continues with a
warning, because the check is only advice (`internal/prereq/prereq.go:128-131`).
**Action:** Nothing, unless the engine later fails to start. Then open a terminal, run `ldd --version`
and include the first line in your report.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:120-139`.

#### 20. `This Linux is too old for the engine (needs glibc 2.38, e.g. Ubuntu 24.04).`

**Message:** `This Linux is too old for the engine (needs glibc <2.34 or 2.38>, e.g. Ubuntu 24.04).`
**Meaning:** The engine's build for your hardware needs a newer C library than this Linux has. The
number is 2.34 for CPU and Vulkan builds, and 2.38 for CUDA and arm64 builds
(`internal/prereq/prereq.go:124-137`).
**Action:** Use a newer Linux release, for example Ubuntu 24.04, and run setup again.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:124-137`.

#### 21. `Couldn't read the driver's CUDA version; EZLM will use the Vulkan engine.`

**Message:** `NVIDIA driver` / `Couldn't read the driver's CUDA version; EZLM will use the Vulkan
engine.`
**Meaning:** The graphics card is there but its driver did not report a CUDA version, so EZLM falls
back to the Vulkan engine. Models still run, more slowly (`internal/prereq/prereq.go:149-151`).
**Action:** Update your NVIDIA driver, then scan again. If it still says this, use Vulkan and ignore
it.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:141-164`.

#### 22. `Your driver is too old for the CUDA engine, so EZLM uses Vulkan (slower). Update your driver for full speed.`

**Message:** exactly as above.
**Meaning:** The driver reports a CUDA version below 12.4, so the CUDA engine cannot be used
(`internal/prereq/prereq.go:151-153`).
**Action:** Install the current NVIDIA driver and scan again.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:151-153`.

#### 23. `Your graphics card needs a newer driver (CUDA 13) for full speed; EZLM uses Vulkan until then.`

**Message:** exactly as above.
**Meaning:** This card's code only ships in the engine's CUDA 13 builds, and the driver is older than
CUDA 13 (`internal/prereq/prereq.go:153-155`, `:166-178`).
**Action:** Install the current NVIDIA driver and scan again.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:153-155`.

#### 24. `RTX Spark needs driver 616.41 or newer for the CUDA engine.`

**Message:** exactly as above.
**Meaning:** This RTX Spark card needs at least driver 616.41 for the fast engine
(`internal/prereq/prereq.go:155-157`).
**Action:** Install driver 616.41 or newer from NVIDIA, then scan again.
**Code:** `internal/prereq/prereq.go:155-157`.

#### 25. `macOS version: Update to macOS 13.3 or newer in System Settings > General > Software Update.`

**Message:** a setup step line of the form `<check name>: <action>`, for example
`macOS version: Update to macOS 13.3 or newer ...`
**Meaning:** This is how a `fail` check stops setup. EZLM writes the check's name and its action
into the setup log and stops before downloading anything (`internal/app/app.go:656-658`).
**Action:** Do what the action line says, then run setup again.
**Code:** `internal/app/app.go:646-658`.

### Version (`internal/version`)

#### 26. `EZLM says it is up to date, but I expected a newer version`

**Message:** no error. The version line reads `EZLM <version>`, for example `0.1.11-beta`
(`internal/version/version.go:5`, shown in `internal/app/app.go:468`).
**Meaning:** The app and the engine ship together and share one version string, so there is no
separate engine version to compare. Update checks compare this string against release tags such as
`v0.1.11-beta` (`internal/version/version.go:3-5`, `internal/app/settings.go:37`). A build made by
hand from source can carry the same string as a release and still say it is up to date.
**Action:** Compare the version on the page with the release you expected. If they differ, run
`ezlm version` and include its output in your report.
**Code:** `internal/version/version.go:5`; `cmd/ezlm/main.go:195-196`.

### Messages worth rewording (for a14)

- `forbidden` (entry 1): says nothing about which address is right. Suggest
  `Open the Setup page at 127.0.0.1, not localhost or another machine.`
- `streaming unsupported` (entry 4): sounds like a browser fault. Suggest
  `The page lost its live connection. Reload it.`
- `context deadline exceeded` / `context canceled` (entry 12): Go words, not English. Suggest
  `The step took too long` and `You stopped the step`.
- `Couldn't read the glibc version.` (entry 19): says nothing to do. Suggest
  `Couldn't check the system libraries. Setup can continue.`
- The `awake` failure (entry 14) has no message at all. Suggest a log line such as
  `Couldn't keep the computer awake during setup.`

## a12. The apps' own messages (Windows and macOS)

This section covers messages the two desktop apps show themselves, meaning the C# app in
`windows/EZLM` and the Swift app in `macos/Sources/EZLM`. Messages that come from the Go engine
and are shown unchanged (for example `Download failed: ...`) are documented in a09 to a11; this
section only adds what the app says around them.

How to read an entry:

- **Where** is the screen or control that shows the text.
- **Means** is what the app is telling the tester.
- **Do** is the next action, in one sentence.
- **Code** is the line that produces the text. `{braces}` mark a part filled in at run time.

A tester who can quote the exact text can be matched to one entry below. Where Windows and macOS
word the same message differently, both versions are given; that drift is listed in the report.
Text described as a toast is the small line at the bottom of the window that fades after about four
seconds (`windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:100-110`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:1052-1061`).

### Starting up

#### `Something went wrong`
**Where:** full window, instead of the normal first screen (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** EZLM could not finish starting, or a page failed while it was being drawn. The line under
the heading is the specific reason.
**Do:** press Try again first. If the same text comes back, press Report this problem and send it,
or Copy details for support and paste that into a message.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:167-175`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Screens.swift:3-15`

#### `EZLM's engine is missing from the app. Reinstall EZLM.`
**Where:** the failure screen above, on the first start.
**Means:** the `ezlm` engine binary that ships inside the app is not where the app expects it. An
antivirus quarantine or an incomplete copy of the app is the usual cause.
**Do:** install EZLM again over the current copy; the tester's models are kept.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Engine.cs:54`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Engine.swift:37`

#### `Couldn't start EZLM's engine.`
**Where:** the failure screen, Windows only.
**Means:** Windows refused to start the engine process. This is rare and usually an antivirus or
permissions block.
**Do:** press Try again, and if it repeats, add EZLM to the antivirus allow list and reinstall.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Engine.cs:68`

#### `EZLM's engine didn't start within 30 seconds. Your antivirus may be scanning it; try again in a moment.`
**Where:** the failure screen, Windows. macOS shows `EZLM's engine didn't start within 30 seconds. Try again in a moment.`
**Means:** the engine was started but did not answer within 30 seconds. A first run on a slow disk
or a real-time antivirus scan is the usual cause.
**Do:** wait a few seconds and press Try again. If it keeps happening, allow EZLM in the antivirus
and try once more.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Engine.cs:75`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Engine.swift:69`

#### `EZLM's engine stopped while starting. Your antivirus may have blocked it.`
**Where:** the failure screen, Windows. macOS shows `EZLM's engine stopped while starting.`
**Means:** the engine process exited before it said it was ready. Windows adds the antivirus hint
because a blocked binary is the common cause there.
**Do:** press Try again, then check the antivirus quarantine for `ezlm.exe` and reinstall if it is
listed.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Engine.cs:76`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Engine.swift:76`

#### `EZLM's engine sent an address it can't use.`
**Where:** the failure screen, macOS only.
**Means:** the engine started but reported a local address the app could not parse. This is a bug,
not something the tester did.
**Do:** press Try again and then Report this problem so the address reaches the developers.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/Engine.swift:90`

#### `EZLM's background engine stopped unexpectedly. Your model server keeps running; Try again reconnects to it.`
**Where:** the failure screen, after the app was already open (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the engine crashed while the window was open. The model server is a separate process and
is still serving the tester's apps.
**Do:** press Try again to reconnect. Chat and model switching are unavailable until it reconnects.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:185`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:286`

#### `This page hit a problem and couldn't be shown.`
**Where:** the body of one section, under its heading, Windows only.
**Means:** one page threw an error while drawing. The rest of the window still works, and the
reason is shown under this line.
**Do:** press Try again, or move to another section and come back. Copy details for support if it
happens on the same page twice.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:673-675`

### Setting up or switching a model

#### `Setup failed.`
**Where:** the setup or switch screen, under the steps (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the setup job stopped without giving a reason. This is the fallback; usually the engine
sends a specific line instead, and that line replaces this one.
**Do:** press Back to the start and run the setup again. If the same step fails, use Report this
problem on the same panel.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Install.cs:225`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:612`

#### The line under a failed setup
**Where:** the setup or switch screen, under the red reason. One of four sentences is shown.
**Means:** what state the computer was left in.
**Do:** follow the sentence, then retry.

- `Nothing was changed on your computer except what was downloaded, which is kept for next time.`
  The tester was setting up from the first-run screen. Run the setup again; the download resumes.
- `{model} is back and running, so your apps keep working.` The old model was restored. Connected
  apps keep working while the tester tries again.
- `{model} is back and loading; it'll answer in a minute.` The old model is loading. Wait for
  Overview to say Ready before trying again.
- `Your server is stopped. Press Start server on Overview to bring it back.` Nothing is serving.
  Go to Overview and press Start server.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Install.cs:159-162`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:649-661`

#### `Cancelled. What was already downloaded is kept: it picks up where it stopped next time.`
**Where:** a toast after pressing Cancel during setup (Windows and macOS). When the tester was
switching a model that was already running, a second sentence follows: ` Your model kept running.`
**Means:** the tester stopped the job. Nothing was deleted.
**Do:** start the same model again when ready; the download resumes.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Install.cs:210`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:592`

#### `Make room for this model?`
**Where:** a dialog before setup, Windows only. The body ends with `You can also cancel and free up space yourself.` and the main button is `Make room and continue`.
**Means:** the model does not fit on the disk, so EZLM will remove models the tester is not using,
oldest first, before downloading.
**Do:** press Make room and continue, or Cancel and delete files first. Nothing is removed until
the button is pressed.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Install.cs:102-112`

#### `No model fits in the memory that's free right now. Quit an app on the right, then scan again.`
**Where:** the model chooser, in place of the model list (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** every model needs more memory than is free at this moment. This is about memory, not
disk, and not about the computer being too small.
**Do:** quit a large app from the list on the right, then press Scan again.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:410`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Wizard.swift:190-191`

### The server on Overview

#### `The server couldn't start`
**Where:** the status card on Overview (Windows and macOS). The line under it starts with the
engine's reason.
**Means:** the model server exited while starting. The reason is the engine's own text.
**Do:** press Start server again. On Windows the line ends `Try Start server again; if it keeps
happening, use Copy details for support in Logs.`; on macOS it ends `Try Start server again; if it
keeps happening, report the problem so it can be fixed.`
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Panes.cs:318-319`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/MainView.swift:303-310`

#### `The server is stopped`
**Where:** the status card on Overview, when there is no start error (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the tester stopped the server, or EZLM did after a failed setup.
**Do:** press Start server. The line under it reads `Apps can't reach your model until you start it again.`
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Panes.cs:318-322`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/MainView.swift:322`

#### `EZLM can't control this server right now`
**Where:** a gold panel at the top of Overview (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the model server was started by something else with administrator rights, so EZLM can
stop it or switch models only after a restart. It still answers for the tester's apps.
**Do:** restart the computer, or end `llama-server` in Task Manager (Windows) or Activity Monitor
(macOS), and let EZLM start it again.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Panes.cs:140-141`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/MainView.swift:237-238`

#### `Running on the processor`
**Where:** a gold panel at the top of Overview (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the graphics card refused the model, so it runs on the processor, which is slower.
**Do:** install a newer graphics driver, then press Try the graphics card again. The panel body
reads `Your graphics card couldn't load this model ({reason}), so it runs on the processor, slower
than it could be. A newer graphics driver may fix this.`
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Panes.cs:147-151`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/MainView.swift:216-224`

### Chat

#### `It didn't answer. Try asking again.`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the reply finished with no text and no error.
**Do:** ask again. If every question does this, check Overview and start the server if it is stopped.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Chat.cs:668`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:298`

#### `It thought about it but didn't write an answer. Try asking again.`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat.
**Means:** the model used its thinking budget and then stopped before writing a reply.
**Do:** ask again, or ask a shorter question.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Chat.cs:668`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:298`

#### `Couldn't reach your model. It may have stopped: check Overview.`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat.
**Means:** the app could not connect to the model server at all.
**Do:** open Overview and press Start server if it is stopped, then ask again.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Chat.cs:671`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:306-307`

#### `Your model stopped in the middle of answering. Check Overview, then ask again.`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat.
**Means:** the connection dropped after the reply started. The partial text is kept.
**Do:** check Overview, start the server if needed, and ask again.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Chat.cs:672`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:306`

#### `Something went wrong: {details}`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat.
**Means:** an unexpected error while reading the reply. The details are the operating system's text.
**Do:** ask again. If it repeats, press Report this problem and include what was being asked.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Chat.cs:673`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:309`

#### `Your model is still loading. Try again in a moment.`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat.
**Means:** the server answered with "loading" or status 503, which happens just after a start or a
model switch.
**Do:** wait for Overview to say Ready, then ask again.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ChatStore.cs:253`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:700`

#### `The server didn't accept EZLM's key. Restart EZLM; if it keeps happening, report a problem.`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat.
**Means:** the app's key and the server's key no longer match, usually after a restart of one but
not the other.
**Do:** quit and open EZLM again. If it repeats, report it.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ChatStore.cs:254`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:701`

#### `That's more than the model can read at once, even with older messages left out. Try a shorter message or file.`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat.
**Means:** the question plus the attached text is larger than the model's context, even after EZLM
drops older turns.
**Do:** send a shorter message, or attach a smaller part of the file.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ChatStore.cs:252`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:699`

#### `Your model answered with an error ({code}): {message}`
**Where:** under the tester's message in Chat.
**Means:** the server returned an error EZLM has no plain sentence for. The code and message are
shown as the server sent them.
**Do:** ask again. If the same code comes back, copy the line into a problem report.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ChatStore.cs:255`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:702`

#### Attaching a file to a chat
**Where:** a toast at the bottom of the window when a file is added.
**Means and action, by text:**

- `{name} is too big to attach ({size} MB). Copy in the part you need instead.` The file is over
  2 MB. Paste the relevant part into the message instead.
- `EZLM can't read {name} yet: PDF and Word files need their text copied in.` PDF and DOCX are not
  read yet. Copy the text into the message.
- `{name} isn't a text file, so the model can't read it.` The file is binary. Attach a text file.
- `{name} is about {tokens} tokens: more than {model} can keep in mind ({limit}).` The file is too
  large for the model's context. Attach a smaller part.
- `Couldn't read {name}: {details}` (Windows) or `Couldn't read {name}.` (macOS). The file could
  not be opened, usually because another app has it locked.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Chat.cs:1037-1052`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ChatModel.swift:484-494`

### Connecting and opening apps

#### `Couldn't open {app}.`
**Where:** the line under a launch button, and a toast (Windows). macOS shows `Couldn't open it.` in
the same place.
**Means:** the app was installed and connected but did not start. The engine usually supplies a
more specific sentence, which replaces this one.
**Do:** press the launch button again. If it repeats, open the app by hand to check it starts, then
use Report this problem.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ReportLaunch.cs:92`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ReportLaunch.swift:46`

#### `Couldn't read the log: {details}`
**Where:** a toast when Show details is pressed on an app tile, Windows only.
**Means:** the app's connection log could not be fetched from the engine.
**Do:** press Show details again. If it repeats, the engine has stopped, so press Try again on the
failure screen.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ReportLaunch.cs:129`

#### `Hermes needs a 64K context, which {model} can't have on this computer. Switch to a smaller model to use it with Hermes.`
**Where:** the Hermes tile on Connect, in gold (Windows and macOS). The tile cannot be selected
while this is true.
**Means:** the model is too large to reserve a 64K context for, and Hermes requires one.
**Do:** switch to a smaller model, then connect Hermes again.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Panes.cs:576`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:906`

#### `This model can't use tools, so {app} can't edit files with it. Pick a model marked Tools, or use Chat.`
**Where:** the status line on an app tile (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the connected model does not support tool calling, which OpenCode, Hermes and DeepSeek
Harness need to edit files.
**Do:** pick a model marked Tools in Models, or use the built-in Chat instead.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Models.cs:188`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Models.swift:213`

#### `Couldn't open last time` and `The last check failed: {reason}`
**Where:** the status line on an app tile (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the previous launch of that app failed. The first form is used when the app closed right
after opening; the second carries the check's reason.
**Do:** press the app's button to try again, and use Report this problem if it fails the same way.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/Models.cs:189`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Models.swift:215`

#### `{app} didn't close.`
**Where:** Model mode, the step for one app, macOS only. Windows asks `Quit {app}?` in a dialog
instead.
**Means:** the app ignored the request to quit, usually because it has an unsaved document.
**Do:** press Try again, or Keep it to move on without closing that app.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/ModelMode.swift:134`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ModelMode.swift:253-257`,
`windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:494`

#### `{app} is still running (it may have asked to save something, or it keeps going in the background).`
**Where:** Model mode, the step for one app, macOS only. For a background program the text is
`{app} has no window to close.`
**Means:** the app did not exit on the polite request. The next line reads `Force-closing stops it
right away: anything unsaved in it is lost.`
**Do:** press Force close {app} if the tester has saved their work, or Keep it.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/ModelMode.swift:246-251`

### Updates

#### `Couldn't start the installer: {details}`
**Where:** the update note in Settings, Windows only.
**Means:** the downloaded installer could not be started. The details are the Windows error.
**Do:** press Update now again. If it repeats, download the installer from the releases page and run
it by hand.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/SettingsPane.cs:311`

#### `The update didn't download.`
**Where:** the update note in Settings (Windows and macOS). `Update cancelled.` appears instead if
the tester stopped it.
**Means:** the update job ended without a downloaded file and without a more specific reason.
**Do:** press Update now again; a partial download resumes.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/SettingsPane.cs:319`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Settings.swift:56`

#### `The update downloaded, but EZLM can't find the file. Try again.`
**Where:** the update note in Settings, macOS only.
**Means:** the download finished but the disk image is not at the path the engine reported.
**Do:** press Update now again.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/Settings.swift:74`

#### `Drag EZLM into Applications to replace the old one, then open it again.`
**Where:** the update note in Settings, macOS only, after the automatic install failed.
**Means:** the app could not replace itself in place, usually because it is not in Applications or
the folder is not writable. The downloaded disk image is opened in Finder so the tester can drag.
**Do:** drag EZLM from the open window into Applications and confirm Replace, then open EZLM again.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/Settings.swift:96-101`, reason logged by
`macos/Sources/EZLM/Updater.swift:21-58`

#### `Installed. Quit EZLM and open it again to finish.`
**Where:** the update note in Settings, macOS only.
**Means:** the new app is in place but the automatic restart could not be arranged.
**Do:** quit EZLM and open it again from Applications.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/Settings.swift:88-91`

#### `Demo: the update downloaded, but nothing is installed in demo mode.`
**Where:** a toast in Settings when the app runs with `--demo`, macOS only. Windows demo mode has no
update path.
**Means:** demo builds do not install updates.
**Do:** nothing; this is expected in a demo.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/Settings.swift:70-72`

#### `EZLM is running from the download, so it won't be here after a restart. Drag it into Applications.`
**Where:** a gold bar at the top of the window and in the first-run screens, macOS only.
**Means:** the app is running from the disk image or from a translocated copy in Downloads. It works
but will not survive a restart and cannot update itself.
**Do:** press Open Applications and drag EZLM into that folder.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/Settings.swift:424-437`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/Wizard.swift:100`,
`macos/Sources/EZLM/MainView.swift:146`

### Settings and model storage

#### `Couldn't change where models are saved.`
**Where:** a toast in Settings, Windows only.
**Means:** the storage move or save job failed without a more specific line.
**Do:** try Save again, and pick a folder on a disk with enough free space.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/SettingsPane.cs:237`

#### `Couldn't open the folder picker: {details}`
**Where:** a toast in Settings, Windows only.
**Means:** the Windows folder dialog could not open.
**Do:** press Choose a folder again. If it repeats, restart EZLM.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/SettingsPane.cs:216`

#### `Models are already saved there.`
**Where:** a toast in Settings, macOS only.
**Means:** the chosen folder is the one already in use, so nothing was moved.
**Do:** nothing; pick a different folder if a move was intended.
**Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/Settings.swift:170`

### Reporting a problem

#### `Couldn't send the report: {details}`
**Where:** a toast on the report form (Windows and macOS). macOS shows this only when the GitHub
page could not be filled in either.
**Means:** the engine could not take the report and the fallback page could not be built.
**Do:** copy the text of the report and send it to the tester's contact by hand.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ReportLaunch.cs:206`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ReportLaunch.swift:252`

#### `Your report is filled in on GitHub: press Submit there to send it.`
**Where:** a toast after pressing Send on the report form (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the engine could not post the report itself, so a browser page was opened with the text
filled in. Nothing is sent until Submit is pressed.
**Do:** press Submit in the browser tab, then close it.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ReportLaunch.cs:203`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ReportLaunch.swift:243`

#### `Sent. Thank you! (report #{number})`
**Where:** a toast after pressing Send on the report form (Windows and macOS).
**Means:** the report reached the server. The number identifies it in a follow-up message.
**Do:** nothing.
**Code:** `windows/EZLM/ReportLaunch.cs:199`, `macos/Sources/EZLM/ReportLaunch.swift:238`

### Messages that appear only in the log

Some failures have no on-screen text of their own; the app writes them to its log and shows a
generic line instead. Testers who press Copy details for support include the log.

- macOS update install reasons: `EZLM isn't running from an app ({path})`, `The update doesn't
  contain EZLM.app`, `The update is a different app ({id})`, and `{tool} failed: {output}`. The
  screen shows `Drag EZLM into Applications...` for all of them.
  **Code:** `macos/Sources/EZLM/Updater.swift:21-58`
- Engine and page errors on Windows go to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\EZLM\app.log`; on macOS they go to the
  in-app log shown under Logs. **Code:** `windows/EZLM/Shell.cs:192-204`,
  `macos/Sources/EZLM/AppModel.swift:1025`

### Notes for the assembler

- Every entry has the three parts in the order message, meaning, action.
- The two apps share most sentences word for word. The exceptions are listed in
  `agents/T13/a12/REPORT.md` under drift, and should be shown per platform if space allows.
- Messages from the engine are not repeated here. If an entry's text starts with a capital and
  names a file, a model or a URL, check a09 to a11 before adding it to TROUBLESHOOTING.
